_why:
Where a recorded step is cut into more than one slide, so the clicker drives it beat by beat instead of the presenter standing in front of a two-minute film with no way to stop it. PowerPoint cannot pause a video on a click without spending a click on it, so a beat is a slide: the film ends holding the frame the show was waiting on, the click opens the next slide, and the recording carries on from the same frame.

Markers, not timecodes, for the reason cast-split.py cuts steps by their headers: re-recording the show has to move every boundary without anything here being retyped. Two kinds.

  gate:<label>  the driver's own click prompt -- `[->] click to apply it`. The cut lands where the prompt was ANSWERED, which is where the presenter pressed the button when this was recorded. These are free: the recording is already standing still at that frame, so the join is invisible.

  text:<regex>  the first time something appears on screen inside the step. For the beats nobody clicked through -- a pod going CrashLoopBackOff, a node counter moving -- where the scene changes on its own and the slide should change with it.

Optional per entry: "nth" to take the second or third hit instead of the first, and "title", which is what the notes pane calls the slide.

0.at: gate:click for the one thing you need
0.title: The one thing before incident 1

1.2.at: gate:click to move a week forward
1.2.title: A week later, boot got slower

1.3.at: gate:click to see what kubelet said
1.3.title: What kubelet said

1.4.title: The probe goes back to its job

1.4.at: gate:click to start the same traffic again
1.4.title: The same load, again

2.2.at: gate:click when you are done talking
2.2.title: The queue fills

2.4.at: gate:click to fill the queue again
2.4.title: The same queue, again
